prompt.context_jp: 晴れた休日の午後、居間には親子三人だけの静かな時間___流れていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 居間には親子三人だけの静かな時間___流れていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that best fits this scene-setting sentence.

feedback.correct_en: This opens the chapter by introducing a brand-new scene — the quiet time itself is fresh information presented to the reader, so が is natural.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would turn 静かな時間 into a known topic, but nothing earlier has established it. を doesn't fit because 流れる here is intransitive.

contrast_examples.jp: 静かな時間が流れていた。
contrast_examples.en: A quiet time was flowing. (newly introduced)

contrast_examples.jp: その時間はあっという間に過ぎた。
contrast_examples.en: That time (already known) passed in a flash.

prompt.context_jp: お父さんの血を引いてるから半分宇宙人ってことになるかな。
prompt.prompt_jp: 孝介は地球で生まれて地球で育ってるから地球人で___あるんだけど、お父さんの血を引いてるから半分宇宙人ってことになるかな。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits this 'yes, but…' nuance?

feedback.correct_en: で+は concedes one point (yes, you are an Earthling) while setting up a contrast (but you're also half-alien). This contrastive は is exactly what the father is doing here.
feedback.incorrect_en: で+が would just assert existence without setting up contrast. で+も would mean 'is an Earthling too,' which doesn't fit the explanation.

contrast_examples.jp: 好きではあるけど、結婚はしない。
contrast_examples.en: I do like him, but I won't marry him.
I like him, so I'll marry him. (no contrast)

prompt.context_jp: 恭介は妻に代わって答えを引き取ろうとしたが…
prompt.prompt_jp: 綾乃の落ち着き払った表情のほう___早かった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits 'it was Ayano's calm expression that was quicker'?

feedback.correct_en: This is an exhaustive-listing が — of the two possibilities (Kyousuke speaking vs. Ayano's expression), Ayano's was the one that was quicker. が picks out the winner.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make 'Ayano's expression' the topic and lose the sense of 'it was X that was quicker.' に doesn't fit syntactically.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼女のほうが早かった。
contrast_examples.en: She was the quicker one. (picks the winner)
She was quick. (just describing her)

prompt.context_jp: 「でも その代わり…」
prompt.prompt_jp: お母さん___優しいだろう？
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits here?

feedback.correct_en: Mom has just been established as the topic (母さんは…). The father continues talking ABOUT her — a classic topic は. There's also an implicit contrast with 'super powers': she doesn't have those, but she IS kind.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would sound like you're newly identifying who is kind, which doesn't match the flow. も would mean 'Mom is kind too,' implying someone else just mentioned was kind.

contrast_examples.en: Mom is kind. (talking about her)
It's Mom who's the kind one. (identifying)

prompt.context_jp: ちょうど夕飯の時間。
prompt.prompt_jp: 食卓に湯気___立ちのぼり、味噌汁の匂いが部屋に満ちた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits this descriptive scene?

feedback.correct_en: The steam is new information observed in the scene — a classic 'something happens / exists' event. Narrative description of sensory events uses が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would mark 湯気 as a pre-established topic, which it isn't. を would need a transitive verb, but 立ちのぼる is intransitive.

contrast_examples.en: Steam rose up. (observed event)
As for steam, it wasn't visible. (contrastive)

prompt.context_jp: 綾乃がふたりの食べ方を気にして言う。
prompt.prompt_jp: いつもより箸___進んでなくない？
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: 箸が進む is a set collocation ('chopsticks move forward' = eating well). The subject of this fixed expression takes が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would break the idiomatic flow and sound like she's singling out chopsticks for contrast with something else — not her intent.

contrast_examples.en: A dish that makes you eat and eat.
Today I don't have much appetite.

prompt.context_jp: 二人は視線を逸らしてごまかそうとする。
prompt.prompt_jp: だが恭介の鼻___ごまかせない。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits this contrastive turn?

feedback.correct_en: だが signals a contrast: they can trick their faces, but Kyousuke's nose — specifically — can't be fooled. This is textbook contrastive は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark the nose as a neutral new subject and lose the 'but THIS one…' contrast. を is wrong because 鼻 is the subject of a potential-form verb here.

contrast_examples.jp: 目はごまかせても、鼻はごまかせない。
contrast_examples.en: You can trick the eyes, but not the nose.
He has a sharp nose. (neutral description)

prompt.context_jp: 居間に戻ってきた孝介が目にした光景。
prompt.prompt_jp: テーブルには湯呑___ひとつ増えていて、綾乃が黙ってお茶を注いでいる。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: The extra teacup is a newly-noticed detail in the scene. Existential/appearance verbs like 増える with brand-new referents take が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would require 湯呑 to be a pre-established topic, but Kousuke is just now noticing it. に is already used earlier in the sentence for location.

contrast_examples.en: A chair was added. (newly noticed)
As for chairs, there are three. (giving info about them)

prompt.context_jp: 父が語った副作用の話は、幼い孝介の胸にはうまく収まらなかったが…
prompt.prompt_jp: 封印という言葉だけ___妙に耳の奥に残った。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits here?

feedback.correct_en: だけは sets up a sharp contrast: the rest of the story slipped away, but ONLY the word '封印' stuck. This 'only X, in contrast' use is contrastive は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が wouldn't carry the 'in contrast to all the rest' nuance that だけは delivers. を is syntactically wrong — 残る is intransitive.

contrast_examples.jp: 名前だけは覚えている。
contrast_examples.en: I remember just the name (and nothing else).
I can't recall the name. (neutral)

prompt.context_jp: 綾乃が廊下に出たそのとき…
prompt.prompt_jp: 玄関の呼び鈴___控えめに鳴った。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: The doorbell ringing is a sudden new event in the narrative — a classic 'that moment, something happened' sentence. が marks this fresh event-subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make the doorbell a known topic, which breaks the surprise of the ring. で would mean 'at/with the doorbell,' which doesn't make sense.

contrast_examples.en: The phone rang. (sudden event)
As for the phone, it didn't ring. (contrast)

prompt.context_jp: 三人の視線が一枚の紙に注がれる。
prompt.prompt_jp: 封筒を破る音___、やけに大きく響いた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: The sound of tearing is a sudden sensory event in the tense moment. Narrative description of a sound suddenly resonating uses が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would frame the sound as a known topic being commented on, losing the immediacy. を is wrong because 響く is intransitive.

contrast_examples.jp: ドアを閉める音が響いた。
contrast_examples.en: The sound of a door closing echoed. (event)

contrast_examples.jp: その音はもう聞こえない。
contrast_examples.en: That sound is no longer audible. (known topic)

prompt.context_jp: 父が能力の副作用を警告していた場面を受けて。
prompt.prompt_jp: 父の警告___決して大袈裟ではなかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: The father's warning has been the whole topic of the preceding scene. The narrator now evaluates it: 'as for that warning, it wasn't an exaggeration.' That's topic は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would freshly introduce the warning as new, but it's already the ongoing topic. も would mean 'the warning too,' needing a prior comparable item.

contrast_examples.jp: 父の警告は本当だった。
contrast_examples.en: Dad's warning was true. (commenting on it)
A warning came from Dad. (new event)

prompt.context_jp: 母が振り向いて何かを言おうとした その瞬間…
prompt.prompt_jp: 道路のほうから鈍いブレーキ音___した。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: 音がする ('a sound occurs') is a fixed existence/occurrence pattern. The subject of this pattern is always marked with が when the sound is newly perceived.
feedback.incorrect_en: 音はした would suggest contrast with something — 'at least the sound happened (though…).' That isn't the meaning here. を is wrong because する here is intransitive.

contrast_examples.en: I heard a strange sound. (new event)
There was no sound (contrast implied).

prompt.context_jp: 彼女たちと出会ってから…
prompt.prompt_jp: 孝介の日々の色合い___確かに変わり始めていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: This is a reflective narration about Kousuke's life as the ongoing topic. '確かに' ('certainly') also pairs naturally with a topic-は comment.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would freshly introduce 日々の色合い, but it's being framed as something we're reflecting on. で doesn't make syntactic sense here.

contrast_examples.en: His life has changed. (comment on known topic)
Something changed. (new, unspecified)

prompt.context_jp: みずぽんが超能力者だと由美が告げた直後。
prompt.prompt_jp: 由美の何気ないひと言___、テーブルの空気を一瞬で塗り替えた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: The sentence highlights the striking impact Yumi's remark had — 'it was Yumi's remark that transformed the atmosphere.' が picks out the agent of this sudden effect.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make the remark a background topic and dilute the impact. を is wrong because this slot is the subject, not the object (the object is 空気).

contrast_examples.jp: 彼女のひと言が場を変えた。
contrast_examples.en: Her one remark changed the mood. (dramatic subject)

contrast_examples.jp: 彼女のひと言は印象的だった。
contrast_examples.en: Her remark was impressive. (describing it)

prompt.context_jp: 父が能力について語る場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: お父さんは その力は ___ようにしてるんだよ。
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb fits — 'I'm trying not to ___ my power'?

feedback.correct_en: 〜ないようにする means 'make a point of not doing.' The father chooses not to use his power — a volitional restraint, not an inability.
feedback.incorrect_en: 使えない (can't use) would mean he's incapable, but he just demonstrated the power. 使わせない (not let someone use) doesn't fit — he's talking about himself.

contrast_examples.jp: 甘いものは食べないようにしている。
contrast_examples.en: I try not to eat sweets. (self-restraint)

contrast_examples.jp: 甘いものは食べられない。
contrast_examples.en: I can't eat sweets. (inability)

prompt.context_jp: 父が孝介に、能力を使うなと念押しする。
prompt.prompt_jp: 孝介も その力は 今日で___な。
prompt.prompt_en: Which word fits — 'from today, we ___ your power'?

feedback.correct_en: 封印 ('sealing away') is the key word of this chapter — the father wants Kousuke to lock away his powers. The chapter title 力の封印 itself uses this word.
feedback.incorrect_en: 発揮 means 'exhibit/display' — the opposite of what he's asking. 解禁 means 'lift the ban,' also the opposite.

contrast_examples.en: Seal away one's powers.
Exert one's powers.

prompt.context_jp: 宇宙服のような服で散歩して怪しまれた話のあと。
prompt.prompt_jp: ごめん ___してた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which word fits — 'Sorry, I ___'?

feedback.correct_en: 油断する means 'to let one's guard down.' The father admits he got careless about the silver suit standing out — exactly this nuance.
feedback.incorrect_en: 安心する ('feel relieved') and 心配する ('worry') don't match an apology for carelessness.

contrast_examples.en: Carelessness is your worst enemy.

contrast_examples.jp: 一瞬の油断が事故を招く。
contrast_examples.en: A moment's lapse invites accidents.

prompt.context_jp: 父が「能力を使ってないよな？」と疑ったのに対し、母が擁護する。
prompt.prompt_jp: ヤダ 何言ってんの ___に決まってるじゃん ねえ？
prompt.prompt_en: Which word fits — 'Of course he got in ___'?

feedback.correct_en: 自力 ('one's own effort') contrasts with 'using powers.' Mom insists he passed through his own ability, not supernatural help — this word reappears later (「自力で リベンジしようと思った」).
feedback.incorrect_en: 他力 ('relying on others') would mean the opposite. 実力 means 'actual ability,' which is close but doesn't carry the 'did it myself, no cheating' nuance that answers the father's suspicion.

contrast_examples.en: I passed under my own power.
You can't just rely on others.

prompt.context_jp: ズルして大学に受かった代償でハゲた、という流れを受けて。
prompt.prompt_jp: ___が当たったんですね。
prompt.prompt_en: Which word fits — 'that's ___ (karma) for you'?

feedback.correct_en: バチが当たる is the set expression for 'getting punished (by heaven/fate) for a misdeed.' It fits the teasing 'that's karma' comment perfectly.
feedback.incorrect_en: 運が当たる isn't a set phrase (運がいい/悪い is used instead). 縁が当たる is not an expression at all.

contrast_examples.jp: 悪いことをするとバチが当たるよ。
contrast_examples.en: If you do bad things, karma will catch you.
I was just lucky.

prompt.context_jp: レイクホテルの警備が厳しくなっても…
prompt.prompt_jp: 俺が なんとか セキュリティーを___ タンクにお湯を入れて 持ち帰ったりしてた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb fits — 'I managed to ___ security'?

feedback.correct_en: かいくぐる specifically means to slip through/evade (a net, security, watchful eyes). It's the exact verb for sneaking past guards.
feedback.incorrect_en: 飛び越える ('leap over') and 乗り越える ('overcome / climb over') are too literal/physical, and 乗り越える usually implies hardship, not stealth.

contrast_examples.jp: 警備の目をかいくぐる。
contrast_examples.en: Slip past the guards' eyes.
Overcome hardship.

prompt.context_jp: 母が車にはねられた瞬間を振り返って。
prompt.prompt_jp: 絶対 能力は使っちゃいけないって ずっと封印してきたからさ ___なくて…
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb fits — 'I couldn't ___'?

feedback.correct_en: 反応する means to react instinctively/physically to a sudden stimulus. In the split-second car-crash moment, this is the natural verb.
feedback.incorrect_en: 返事する is 'reply (to speech),' and 対応する usually implies deliberate handling of a situation, not an instant reflex to danger.

contrast_examples.jp: とっさに反応できなかった。
contrast_examples.en: I couldn't react in the moment.
Deal with the problem.

prompt.context_jp: 三人の存在が孝介の胸に…
prompt.prompt_jp: 静かな灯を___始めていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb collocates with 灯 ('light / lamp')?

feedback.correct_en: 灯をともす is the literary collocation for 'light a lamp / kindle a light,' often used metaphorically for warmth in the heart. It fits this reflective passage.
feedback.incorrect_en: 灯をつける is possible but much more everyday (flipping a switch). 灯を開く is not a natural collocation.

contrast_examples.en: Kindle a light in one's heart. (literary)
Turn on the light. (everyday)

prompt.context_jp: 綾乃が廊下に出た、その瞬間に起きた出来事を描写したい。
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds more natural as narrative description?

choices.text: そのとき、玄関の呼び鈴が控えめに鳴った。
そのとき、玄関の呼び鈴は控えめに鳴った。

feedback.correct_en: For a sudden, newly-introduced event in narration, が is the natural choice — the bell is appearing in the scene for the first time.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would frame the doorbell as something we were already discussing, which is odd for an unexpected ring breaking the moment.

contrast_examples.en: The door opened. (event, natural)

contrast_examples.jp: そのドアは開かなかった。
contrast_examples.en: That door (specifically) didn't open. (contrast)

prompt.context_jp: 清美に『天国のお母さん』と言われた孝介の反応。
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds more natural as Kousuke's blunt, exasperated correction?

choices.text: あのさ… 死んでねえから。
あのう、まだ亡くなっておりませんので。

feedback.correct_en: The scene is a casual chat among coworkers, and Kousuke bluntly cuts off the mistaken condolence. 死んでねえ (contracted ない) matches his teasing, deflating tone.
feedback.incorrect_en: The polite 亡くなっておりません belongs in business/formal speech. Using it here would be bizarrely stiff for the emotional punchline.

contrast_examples.en: I'm not dead yet. (casual)

contrast_examples.jp: まだお亡くなりになっておりません。
contrast_examples.en: He has not yet passed away. (formal)

prompt.context_jp: 父の副作用の話は幼い孝介にはよく分からなかった、という文脈。
prompt.prompt_en: Which version better conveys 'only the word 封印 stuck in his ears'?

choices.text: 封印という言葉だけは妙に耳の奥に残った。
封印という言葉だけが妙に耳の奥に残った。

feedback.correct_en: だけは pairs 'only X' with contrastive は — the rest faded, but THIS word remained. The contrast with everything else that didn't stick is the point.
feedback.incorrect_en: だけが is grammatical but feels like a neutral listing of 'the one thing that remained,' losing the implicit contrast with everything that didn't.

contrast_examples.jp: 名前だけは覚えている。
contrast_examples.en: At least the name I remember. (contrast)
The name is my only clue. (identifying)

prompt.context_jp: 息子が『ただいま』と帰ってきたときの母の返事。
prompt.prompt_en: Which greeting sounds more natural from a mom to her kid?

choices.text: おかえり！ 手ぇ洗ってうがいしな。
お帰りなさいませ。お手を洗ってうがいをなさってください。

feedback.correct_en: The 'ぇ' in 手ぇ and the imperative-sounding しな are warm, familiar family speech — exactly the register of a mom at home.
feedback.incorrect_en: The second version is hyper-polite keigo you'd use with guests or customers, not with your own child in your own kitchen.

contrast_examples.en: Go wash your hands. (familiar, parent)

contrast_examples.jp: お手洗い場はあちらでございます。
contrast_examples.en: The restroom is over there. (service keigo)

prompt.context_jp: 二人は視線を逸らしてごまかそうとするが、父は鼻がきく。
prompt.prompt_en: Which version best delivers the 'but THIS part can't be fooled' nuance?

choices.text: だが恭介の鼻はごまかせない。
だが恭介の鼻がごまかせない。

feedback.correct_en: だが sets up contrast. は picks out 'the nose, specifically' as the thing that defeats the deception — matching the setup where their faces could be hidden.
feedback.incorrect_en: が in a potential-form negative here sounds like a general statement that his nose can't be deceived, missing the pointed 'but his nose, that part' contrast.

contrast_examples.jp: 目はごまかせても、鼻はごまかせない。
contrast_examples.en: You can trick the eyes but not the nose.
He has a good nose. (neutral)
